title: microstand serving ops — weekly prep (ariella)
content:
Purpose: quick, focused 25–30m micro-stand for serving + infra + console alignment (avoid long slides).
Meeting window: Tue 09:30–10:00 PT (recurring). I'm owning agenda this week.
Attendees (target): infra-oncall, runtime-lead, console-sv, SRE rep, capacity-eng (if available).
Goals for this session:
- Rapidly triage any regressions from last deploy (latency, errors, capacity).
- Confirm go/no-go blockers for console rollout to staging.
- Align on one automation task to reduce manual toil this sprint.
- 3 clear action items with owners and due dates.

Agenda (timed):
1) Quick health + showstoppers (5m) — infra oncall gives top 2 metrics: p99 latency, 5xx rate, queue depth. Call out any customer-facing incidents.
2) Latency regression post-2026-03-08 deploy (8m) — runtime lead to summarize hypothesis, telemetry pointers. Decide whether to rollback or patch.
3) Console rollout status (6m) — console owner to surface: A/B route config, auth edge cases, tracing not showing user ids. Any rollback criteria?
4) Capacity & Dedicated pools (3m) — confirm whether burst capacity toggle acted as expected last night.
5) Action items & parking lot (3m) — assign owners, quick sync on timelines.

Prep notes (things I want ready before the call):
- Have the p99 latency graph up from Grafana (last 72h) and a diff view vs baseline.
- Error tail sample: paste 3 representative 5xx error traces (stack snippets).
- Quick console demo: showing user route missing trace ids (screenshot).
- Link to the failing loadtest run (Jenkins id).

Talking points / prompts to use if discussion stalls:
- "If no single root cause, do we have a guarded rollback plan?"
- "Which customer flows are hit hardest? Prioritize them for mitigation"
- "Can we gate the rollout by a simple health check endpoint?"

Unresolved questions I need answered before Friday:
- Is the new kernel-select logic (PR 1218) feature flagged per model, or global? (affects rollback scope)
- Did the autoscaler observe a sustained CPU plateau between 02:00–03:00 PT last night? (need raw pod metrics)
- Who owns the tracing header mapping change that removed user_id from propagated headers? (console vs runtime)

Action items (tracking — put initials in comments):
- A1: Runtime team to validate PR 1218 can be toggled off without full restart. Owner: Diego Ramos. Due: 2026-03-13. Status: open. Notes: Diego to try feature-flag flip in staging and report side-effects.
- A2: Console team to add a short-circuit health check (probe) that returns 200 only if trace mapping present. Owner: Nora Patel. Due: 2026-03-15. Status: open. Notes: Minimal impl, fallback to previous behavior behind a flag.
- A3: SRE to run focused loadtest for the p99 regression window and attach traces. Owner: Samir Khullar (oncall). Due: 2026-03-14. Status: open. Notes: include full request/response sizes.

Parking lot (if time) / follow-ups:
- Discuss cost impact of continuous small rollouts vs batched releases (optimize for fewer rollbacks).
- Longer-term: instrument per-route quantization profile usage (ops ask).

Personal checklist before call:
- [x] Upload screenshots to meeting doc.
- [ ] Paste latest Grafana links into Slack channel #serving-ops.
- [ ] DM Diego to confirm staging window at 09:00 PT.

Post-meeting follow-up template (copy into meeting notes after close):
- Summary (2 lines)
- Decisions (explicit)
- Action items (owner + due date)
- Blockers & who to escalate to (names + slack links)

Notes to self: keep this microstand <30m. If discussion goes deep, spawn a focused follow-up with a prewritten agenda and only select participants. Use the parking lot bullets above to capture that.

Quick links I referenced in prep (copy into meeting chat):
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/serving/latency-72h
- Jenkins run: https://ci.redwood.internal/job/serving-loadtest/346
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1218

End-of-note.
(Imperative: after meeting, paste concise outcomes into Confluence page linked above and ping Product Ops.)
